8ae540afd0f86fb1.title: Metabolome-wide Association Study of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia in Extremely Premature Infants
digest: Objective: To identify metabolites and pathways altered in infants who develop BPD through a metabolome-wide association study.
Methods: We performed untargeted urinary metabolomics in 314 infants (<29 weeks gestational age) at two time points between postnatal days 5-15 and 23-32, with detailed time-series for 28 infants.
We compared metabolite levels between infants with and without BPD at 36 weeks postmenstrual age using logistic regression and pathway enrichment analysis.

results.verbatim: Results: Among the 913 analyzed urinary metabolites, 23 and 68 were nominally associated with BPD between postnatal days 5-15 and 23-32, respectively (p<0.05).
We found enrichment in the lactoyl amino acid sub-pathway (5-15 days; p=0.005, q=0.4) and xanthine metabolism and fatty acid metabolism (23-32 days; p[≤]0.002, q<0.1).

Most BPD-differential metabolites were lower in infants with BPD at days 23-32 (OR=7.1, p=2x10-6), with similar patterns among infants receiving parenteral (OR=9.2, p=7x10-7) and full enteral nutrition (OR=6.1, p=0.003).
